subject: Post-call: Ranking adapter + infra next steps (SDK / auth / eval checklist)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Choudhury <anita@shopmax.com>
Cc: search-team@shopmax.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Ranking adapter + infra next steps (SDK / auth / eval checklist)

Hi Anita — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of ask (from your side): shop homepage search needs a quality uplift for queries with short contexts (1–3 tokens), better freshness for promotions, and faster tail-latency during peak traffic. You want an approach that doesn't require a full reindex or heavy infra changes.

What we proposed: Redwood Ranking Adapter flow — embedding-based candidate generation (existing Elastic candidates) -> lightweight reranker model served via Redwood Dedicated (quantized) -> structured score output (top_k with scores and rationale tokens). Key infra notes: SDK integration is ~1 week for a single route, auth via API key or service account JWT, and routing we can configure so lower-sla traffic stays on embeddings-only.

Open technical questions I noted (from call):
- Preferred auth model (team prefers IAM/service account for non-prod and API key for analytics jobs)
- Whether we can run a small eval harness against your QA dataset (50 queries sample)
- Production routing: do you want a gradual rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) or instant swap?

Attachments: I attached a short evaluation checklist and a 50-query sample to start.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) You share the sample evaluation queries and a small candidate set export (CSV or JSONL) — ShopMax DevOps or search-team
2) We provide a minimal SDK snippet for your Java service and a service-account onboarding doc (ETA 48 hours) — Redwood
3) Joint run of the offline eval (MRR/NDCG/Recall@k) and a quick qualitative pass (ETA: 3 business days once we have data)

If that sounds right, I’ll loop Marissa (ML infra) and Karthik (solutions) to scope the SDK + reranker config and draft a mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0146

On a side note, if you have constraints around PII in the sample queries, let us know — we can sign an NDA and accept masked payloads.

From: Anita Choudhury <anita@shopmax.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: search-team@shopmax.com, DevOps - ShopMax <devops@shopmax.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Ranking adapter + infra next steps (SDK / auth / eval checklist)

Thanks Jordan — this is great, appreciate the clear path. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Auth: we prefer service-account JWTs for dev/staging pipelines (we can provision a short-lived key pair) and API keys for analytics/backfills. Can Redwood support both?
- Rollout: planning to start with a canary at 5% for the homepage route, because of the promotional spikes. If safe, we’ll expand to 25% after two days and 100% after we confirm metrics.
- Data: I attached a 50-query sample (anonymized) and a small candidate export (first 10 results per query). We also have a CSV of click labels for a subset — will that be useful for supervised tuning?

Questions: 
1) How does Redwood’s reranker expose relevance signals? We need both a top_k list and feature-level explanation tokens for a limited set of queries for debug.
2) For top_k tuning: any guidance on starting values for top_k, candidate pool size, and how we should set the batch size for lowest latency?

I’ve copied DevOps to coordinate access. Next steps from us: confirm service-account details and share a secure upload link (S3 or shared Drive).

—Anita
Head of Search, ShopMax

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Ranking adapter + infra next steps (ShopMax) — need technical scoping

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding thread from Anita at ShopMax. They sent a 50-query anonymized sample + candidate export and ask for: 
- SDK snippet (Java) + auth options (service account JWT + API key)
- Reranker output: top_k + per-item score + small explanation tokens (3–5 tokens max)
- Guidance on top_k, candidate pool, batch sizing to meet 95th percentile latency SLO of 150ms for homepage route

Notes / constraints: ShopMax wants minimal infra changes (prefer Redwood-managed reranker) and will do canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%). They can provide click labels for a small supervised tuning run.

Can you propose: 
A) Concrete SDK integration checklist (server-side Java) including how to attach service account JWTs, retries, and streaming support
B) Reranker config suggestions (model size, quantization, top_k default, candidate pool) and expected latency/cost tradeoffs for Dedicated vs Hosted fallback
C) Offline eval plan with metrics to surface (MRR, NDCG@10, Recall@K, and an error-rate-ish metric for model hallucination) + acceptance thresholds for canary

If you can turn that into a short PDF (checklist + config table) I’ll attach to the reply and set expectation with Anita.

—Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Ranking adapter + infra next steps (ShopMax) — technical scoping

Jordan/Karthik — see notes below; I put together a concise checklist you can send to Anita. I also attached the quick eval checklist and a sample SDK snippet (Java) in my draft.

A) SDK + Auth checklist (server-side Java):
- Add redwood-java-sdk dependency (v0.9.x)
- Create a ServiceAccount credential: upload public key in ShopMax console -> Redwood issues client_id
- Use JWT flow: exchange signed JWT for short-lived token; include token in Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Fallback: API key as env var for analytic/backfill jobs (non-user facing)
- Implement idempotent retry (exponential backoff) and set streaming(context) timeout at 2.5s for homepage route
- Instrument token-level latency tracing (we have hooks to forward to Datadog)

B) Reranker config guidance:
- Model: small-medium cross-encoder (quantized int8) for low-latency rerank; for very tight latency use distilled scoring head only
- Candidate pool: start with top 50 from Elastic; evaluate recall@50 — if recall low, increase to 200
- top_k: default 5 for homepage, expand to 10 for product detail pages
- Batch size: tune for p95 latency; starting point: 8–12 concurrent tokens per GPU for their traffic profile
- Fallback routing: embeddings-only path for non-promotional low-value traffic (configurable by route)

C) Offline eval plan and metrics:
- Metrics: MRR@10, NDCG@10, Recall@50, Precision@5 (for promo relevance), and Delta CTR (if live).
- Acceptance thresholds (canary): +5% MRR or +2 pts NDCG or no more than 1% regression in CTR for seeded queries. If offline metrics look strong, proceed to 5% canary for 48 hours and monitor CTR & latency.
- Qualitative: inspect top 20 failures (where relevance drops vs baseline) and request feature-level explanations for 30 debug queries.

D) Deliverables & ETA:
- SDK snippet + auth doc (48 hours)
- Initial offline eval run (after ShopMax uploads sample): 3 business days
- Canary rollout plan draft (1 business day after eval)

E) Attachments to send: shopmax_rerank_eval_checklist.pdf, sample_queries_50.jsonl (both attached)

Small note on explanation tokens: we can return short rationale tokens (e.g., [brand_match, recency_boost, query_term_overlap]) — these are not full LLM explanations but structured feature indicators for debugging.

—Marissa
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Choudhury <anita@shopmax.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, search-team@shopmax.com, DevOps - ShopMax <devops@shopmax.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Ranking adapter + infra next steps (SDK / auth / eval checklist)

Anita — thanks for the quick reply and for uploading the anonymized sample + candidate dump. Per Marissa’s notes above, attached are the two deliverables: the eval checklist and a Java SDK/auth snippet. Quick answers to your questions: 

- Auth support: yes — we support both service-account JWT exchange and API keys. I included the step-by-step for generating the JWT and where to upload the public key in the doc.
- Reranker signals: our Ranking API returns an ordered list with per-item score, model_confidence, and a short list of rationale tags (3–5) when enabled. That should cover your debug needs without exposing raw model internals.
- Top_k guidance: start with top_k=5, candidate_pool=50. If offline Recall@50 < 0.8 increase pool to 200 and rerun. Marissa’s guidance on batch sizing is included for p95 latency tuning.

Next steps (mutual action plan):
1) ShopMax: confirm service-account pubkey location and give us secure upload link for the full 2k query sample if available (we can operate on just the 50 to start) — ETA 24–48 hours
2) Redwood: run initial offline eval against 50-query sample and return MRR/NDCG/Recall@50 and 20 failure examples — ETA 3 business days after upload
3) Joint: schedule a 30-min technical sync (Marissa + ShopMax Eng) to review failures and finalize canary routing (recommended 5% for 48 hours) — propose Thu 23 Jul 2026 10:00 PT

I’ll wait for confirmation on upload method and meeting time. If we get the 2k export we can also offer a small supervised tune (if they share click labels) and report expected delta.

Cheers,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: shopmax_rerank_eval_checklist.pdf (22 KB), sample_queries_50.jsonl (3 KB)
